newsitem.title: UK: Ushers of Trowbridge rises 12 pct on debut.
newsitem.headline: Ushers of Trowbridge rises 12 pct on debut.

text.p: Regional brewer Ushers of Trowbridge Group Plc made a strong debut on the London Stock Exchange on Monday, jumping more than 12 percent from its offer price.
"We're very pleased -- it's a nice comfortable premium above the issue price. This just reflects that we were sensible with the pricing," said Ushers chief executive Roger North.

The company used the 38.3 million stg net proceeds to retire and reschedule its debt, freeing cash flow to fund expansion, North said. The company simultaneously negotiated a 25 million stg revolving credit facility, he said.

"This give us a lot of headroom, whereas before there were a lot of things we wanted to do but just couldn't find the cash for," North said, adding that Ushers intended to improve 87 of its 541 tied pubs in England and Wales.
"It also gives us a war chest for acquisitions within our trading area."
The offering was almost three times oversubscribed at the offer price of 110p, and mostly placed with UK institutions, said David Charles of lead underwriter Hambros Bank.
By 1500 GMT the shares were up 13.5p to 123-1/2p on volume of 11.3 million.
Ushers of Trowbridge had operating profit of 16.9 million stg on turnover of 65.4 million stg in 1996.
